title: Tech Note: Some Common Problems Encountered When Using 4th Dimension on the Power Macintosh
author: David Adams

historical_commentary.text: This note catalogs common Power Macintosh compatibility problems developers hit when running 4th Dimension in the mid-1990s transition from 68K to PowerPC Macs — Type 11 errors from insufficient memory partitions, memory-allocation differences between RISC PowerPC and CISC 68K code, a WorldScript international text-handling bug, a CommonGround Shortcut extension conflict, general system extension conflicts, and a compiler memory-sizing formula — all of which are entirely obsolete now that classic Mac OS, 68K emulation, WorldScript, and the extension-based system architecture they describe no longer exist on any current Macintosh platform.
related_updates: Classic Mac OS, the 68K-to-PowerPC transition, WorldScript, and INIT/extension-based system architecture have all been fully superseded by Mac OS X and subsequent macOS releases with a completely different memory and process model
Type 11 errors and manual memory-partition sizing are artifacts of classic Mac OS's cooperative, statically-partitioned memory model, replaced by protected virtual memory in Mac OS X
4D's own compiler and memory management have been substantially modernized since 1996, removing the need for the manual memory-sizing formula described here
